capacityConclusion.raised: Verdict: not feasible to recommend as safe on current evidence. The byte/32-assignment architecture remains a possible design, but cap constants and bounded assignment loops alone leave an eight-word histogram, a33-entry population-indexed cost table and unresolved semantic/codec/UI contracts. A larger explicit title design could replace those contracts; byte127 is not proved impossible.

guards: Do not identify0x830E5AD0 as the city table.

Do not call31 a universal invariant across every population writer; Irrigation lacks the local guard.
Do not replace the assignment vector with a guessed31-entry citizen/specialist array or call tile-index masks packed population.
Do not claim full writer, save/network/UI/AI coverage or runtime acceptance.
Do not narrow an above-cap threshold such as999 to a byte; compare operands and persisted threshold storage are separate contracts.
Do not describe surplus citizens as native specialists/entertainers without a value/consumer contract.

Do not assume every candidate population store is real: city owner, assignment value and tile-position indexes are separate.
Do not equate one-byte stream primitives with complete file/wire compatibility.

Cap127 needs coherent pre-narrowing saturation, bounded assignment and lock operations, explicit surplus/default processing, histogram/caller and cost-table policies, downstream intervals and UI/persistence/peer closure. The all-reader/all-writer census is incomplete; exhaustive raw-form searches and a whole mapped-owner candidate pass do not establish semantic completeness.
